commit: 91eef58 (v0.16.0 + RFC-8 bug-half fix), recalibrated with warmup exclusion after round-1 review
box: 16-core reference box (audit 2026-07-28), single-thread BLAS, median of 5 steady reps (1 warmup excluded)
notes: Thresholds are deliberately generous: CI runners are slower and noisier than the reference box, and the gate exists to catch structural regressions (a lost support-compression or cached-W win), not 20% noise. Ratio checks are machine-speed invariant to first order and carry the tighter limits; absolute checks are large multiples of reference-box medians. The tensor benchmark excludes one warmup fit per case (import/cache effects measured at 1.5-3x steady state were the dominant rep-to-rep spread in CI).
ci_observed: First perf-gate run on ubuntu-latest (2026-07-29, n=30k): steady-state medians ~1.2-1.4x this box; steady ratios tensor_multiplier_exact ~4.2, tensor_multiplier_discrete ~3.1 (both ~15% above the reference box), steady rep spreads 2-5%. Headroom to the ratio limits: 1.43x (exact) and 1.6x (discrete) over observed CI values.

tensor_multiplier_exact.note: reference 3.57, CI-observed ~4.2; the pre-arc reversion is 7.2x and MUST trip, so this limit cannot be widened past ~7 - the 1.43x CI headroom is accepted and rests on warmup exclusion keeping steady ratio noise under ~10%

tensor_multiplier_discrete.note: reference 2.64, CI-observed ~3.1; the 3.8x pre-arc discrete multiplier sits inside runner noise of any non-flapping limit, so this check only guards catastrophic tensor-path blowups

absolute_multiple.note: per-case median vs reference-box median; CI-observed medians are ~1.2-1.4x reference, so the 6.6x pre-arc base-exact reversion trips even on a 2-3x slower runner

limit 2.12s: CI-observed median is 1.044s (2x headroom; the full-data fit is far more stable than the sub-second tensor cases), and the 2.48x pre-arc flagship reversion lands at ~2.6s on the observed runner, which trips - a 5x limit would have let it through
